why: Shorter, concrete, actionable (map your bet); neutral and avoids reciting a named framework in bullets.
The first-person scar story with its setup carries the author's own rough voice, which the rules say earns length.
The guess prompt comes after the full setup and points to the next step, so the reveal flows without a split.
Shorter; B's added sentence is a forward hint and A's 'not drafting from a blank page' already carries the point.
B's added sentence is a vague closer; A is tighter.
'Session' is the controlled term and fits the loop vocabulary better than 'run'.
The title states the concept; 'The generalisation' is an abstraction, and A avoids the restated closer.
B adds a made-up concept ('flywheel') and a witty closer, and the extra encode loop clause adds clutter.
Cuts an unnecessary restatement clause.
B's closer is a moralising one-liner; A is neutral.
'Exercise' names what the student recognises; 'prompts' is less precise.
Colon version is tighter and reads naturally; 'this scrollback' is also clearer.
B adds a forward hint to Module 4; A is a plain, shorter statement.
'YOUR real work is the material' is more direct and drops the stiff 'The training runs on'.
B's 'The move is the same every time' is a restating filler sentence; A is shorter.
B adds a forward-hint closer about Phases 3 and 4; cut it.
A names the loop steps concretely (failing test, fix, pass), which is more picturable; the cut in B loses the concrete content.
'It often isn't. It's a draft' is the cleaner, plainer construction with no 'just'; fine either way, B reads smoother.
A's added sentence ('you are not learning them here') is a hedge that adds nothing; B is shorter and neutral.
A invites the student to run the prompts hands-on; B's 'Watch... rather than typing along' makes them passive.
'Three new concerns' is a count that is easy to get wrong; A avoids it and lists the concerns directly.
'Three pressures' matches the three bullets and is concrete; B's 'Pressures' is vaguer.
A's header says when the file is read, with a concrete scheduled-read framing, while B's 'Three agents using the file' is a count that is false (it lists three triggers).
A states a concrete, checkable thing to ask (how MCP tools land in the same set), while B's 'what it leaves out' is vague.
B adds a closer that tells the student what their practice now is; A is shorter and avoids declaring.
Tighter, plain list reads faster, and the added sim/fix/pushback details are concrete first-person voice.
B's added 'This is your side-quest lane' is a restating sentence; A is shorter.
B's opening fragment is a hedged forward hint that adds nothing; A is cleaner.
'Check' fits the act of verifying a proposal better than 'read', which implies reading all of it.
A states the concrete point; B's forest-before-trees is a cute idiom that adds little.
B's title says the claim directly and is neutral; A's 'resets the chain' is a more abstract title.
A's title is an actionable instruction the student can use tomorrow; B just describes a problem.
B is shorter and names the concrete /statusline command instead of vague 'ask Claude'.
A names the ADR plainly; B's 'a future engineer can inspect' is wordier and vaguer.
A's 'The wall' is a made-up concept the author's taste rules explicitly reject; B drops it.
A's title carries a picturable, concrete claim; B's title is more abstract and restates the body.
Shorter header; 'context' is implied and the word adds nothing.
The added closer is a restatement/platitude; cut whole low-value sentences.
Avoids a fixed count in the title, which is a forward hint and breaks if the list changes; same body otherwise.
Gives a concrete, specific instruction for what to ask Claude; B's fragment is vaguer.
The closing line clarifies phases are places, not a pipeline, which is useful orientation for the model.
Permission framing ('you don't need to get it right first time') lands the experiment stance and the why.
Concrete action the student can take, in plain words; B is abstract and unpicturable.
Cleaner list without extra connective sentences and forward hints.
'Alternative' is the plainer word, and A avoids the extra 'gives you the floor' filler and the jargon-flavored 'committed change'.
